knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A planting above the excluded height that comes near an overhead line is excluded. The correct response records the exclusion and refers the work without starting any part of it.
A sharp reduction is a renovation. It is quoted separately and planned over more than one season, because cutting to bare wood may not regrow on some species.
Access must be an authorised method for the height. Improvised access such as chairs or unapproved ladders is unsafe, and work beyond the authorised method is referred.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied mock planting card with a height and a line-proximity note, the learner decides whether the planting is in scope or excluded and records the decision within the assessor's set time.
The learner sets a target height and width with a string line on a mock hedge and checks the line at two intervals while trimming.
The learner produces a written quote for a supplied renovation scenario that separates the renovation from routine trimming and lists the exclusions.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Scope decision record for the mock planting, signed by the assessor.
Assessor observation record of the string-line trimming, including interval checks.
Written quote for the renovation scenario, reviewed by the assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Any cutting of a mock planting identified as excluded during the assessment.
Use of an access method not authorised by the assessor for the mock height.
Any trimming within the simulated exclusion distance of a power line.
